verses.text: At that time, everyone on earth spoke the same language and used the same words.
As they traveled east, they came to a plain in Shinar and settled there.
They said to each other, "Come on, let's make bricks and bake them hard." They used brick instead of stone and tar for mortar.
Then they said, "Come on, let's build a city and a tower reaching into the sky. We'll make a name for ourselves so we don't get scattered across the earth."
Yahweh came down to see the city and tower the people were building.
Yahweh said, "Look, they're one people and speak one language. This is only the beginning. If they keep going, they could carry out whatever they plan.
Come on, let's go down and mix up their language so they can't understand one another."
So Yahweh scattered them from there across the earth, and they stopped building the city.
That's why the city was called Babel: there Yahweh mixed up the language of the whole earth, and from there he scattered the people everywhere.
Here is the family line of Shem: two years after the flood, when Shem was 100, he became the father of Arpachshad.
After Arpachshad was born, Shem lived another 500 years and had other sons and daughters.
Arpachshad was 35 when he became the father of Shelah.
After Shelah was born, Arpachshad lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
Shelah was 30 when he became the father of Eber.
After Eber was born, Shelah lived another 403 years and had other sons and daughters.
Eber was 34 when he became the father of Peleg.
After Peleg was born, Eber lived another 430 years and had other sons and daughters.
Peleg was 30 when he became the father of Reu.
After Reu was born, Peleg lived another 209 years and had other sons and daughters.
Reu was 32 when he became the father of Serug.
After Serug was born, Reu lived another 207 years and had other sons and daughters.
Serug was 30 when he became the father of Nahor.
After Nahor was born, Serug lived another 200 years and had other sons and daughters.
Nahor was 29 when he became the father of Terah.
After Terah was born, Nahor lived another 119 years and had other sons and daughters.
Terah was 70 when he became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran.
Here is Terah's family line: Terah became the father of Abram, Nahor, and Haran. Haran became the father of Lot.
Haran died in the land where he was born, in Ur of the Chaldees, while his father Terah was still alive.
Abram and Nahor both married. Abram's wife was Sarai, and Nahor's wife was Milcah, Haran's daughter; Haran was also Iscah's father.
Sarai couldn't have children; she had no child.
Terah took his son Abram, his grandson Lot (Haran's son), and his daughter-in-law Sarai (Abram's wife). They left Ur of the Chaldees to go to Canaan. They reached Haran and settled there.
Terah lived 205 years, then died in Haran.
